policy.title: Maximising the Utility of Analytic Products
policy.purpose: IC elements shall produce analytic products that customers can easily discover, access, use, and disseminate. Five principles, listed in priority order from highest to lowest.

rule.name: Know your customers (priority 1)
rule.text: Ensure analysts understand the customer's operating environment: required information, timeliness, classification limits, and optimal methods for discovery and dissemination. Determine before publication whether the product targets a specific customer or a general audience.

rule.name: Meet analytic standards (priority 2)
rule.text: Analytic products must give customers insight into source quality and credibility, characterise the uncertainty of judgments, and include context to aid understanding. All products shall adhere to the standards of analytic tradecraft in ICD-203.

rule.name: Produce for tailored re-use (priority 3)
rule.text: Create products for timely dissemination to US customers (federal, state, local, tribal) and, where permitted, partners. When similar credible information is reported at multiple classification levels, use the lowest level to facilitate re-use. Produce tearlines at the lowest classification level that protects sensitive data, sources, methods, and activities. All analytic products must employ proper sourcing in line with ICD-206. Use alternate versions, portion marking, sanitised text, metadata tagging, and tearlines to facilitate tailored re-use. Sanitised products must remain congruent with their higher-classified versions in facts, judgments, confidence levels, and probabilistic language.

rule.name: Make analytic products discoverable and accessible (priority 4)
rule.text: Ensure that customers with proper clearances and approved mission need can discover and access analytic products. At minimum, disseminate products electronically to the Library of National Intelligence or its successor systems.

rule.name: Demonstrate transparency (priority 5)
rule.text: Adhere to the Principles of Intelligence Transparency: enhance public understanding of intelligence activities while protecting sensitive sources and methods.
